query: For initially solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exposed to the premelting and melting regime, the limited understanding of their thermal response prevents clear definition of their usable temperature range and behavior during high-temperature synthesis. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the onset and progression of their phase transition and why? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, relevant boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior nanoparticle studies, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The onset and progression of phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles are governed by grain boundary diffusion and defect formation, which facilitate atomic rearrangement and nucleation of new phases.
generation.intervention: Controlled heating to premelting and melting temperatures with in-situ TEM observation
generation.conditions: Heating rates of 1-10 K/s, temperature range 500-1200°C, inert gas atmosphere
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary diffusion and defect formation
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary diffusion and defect formation facilitate atomic rearrangement and nucleation of new phases
generation.predicted_outcome: A decrease in the onset temperature of phase transition with increasing heating rate, and the formation of a liquid phase at the grain boundaries prior to complete melting of the nanoparticles
generation.baseline: The thermal response of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles without controlled heating or in-situ TEM observation
generation.boundary: The temperature range 500-1200°C and heating rates of 1-10 K/s
generation.uncertainty: The interpretation of the in-situ TEM observations may be challenging, and the results may be influenced by the experimental conditions
